record.program_name: Housing Opportunities Overlay (Zoning Code 7-9-44), Affordable Housing Permit (7-9-124.3) and density bonus (7-9-87)
record.administering_agency: OC Public Works, OC Development Services, Planning Division (Deysi Munoz, 714-667-8815, Deysi.munoz@ocpw.ocgov.com)
record.typical_award_size: The 2024 Housing Opportunities Overlay Manual allows 100% affordable rental or ownership projects, emergency shelters, multi-service centers and low-barrier navigation centers by right in commercial and industrial districts and on listed residential arterial parcels in the unincorporated area, approved through a ministerial Affordable Housing Permit. Qualified projects must be 100% affordable to low and very low income households (at or below 80% AMI) with at least 30% of units for very low income households; the County NOFA's Attachment J lists eligible sites. Density bonus (Sec. 7-9-87.1 to 87.4) follows Government Code 65915 for bonus amounts, incentives, concessions and waivers; the Mixed-Use district allows 12 feet of extra height as a bonus incentive. No county inclusionary housing ordinance or in-lieu fee.
record.affordability_requirement: Overlay projects: 100% affordable, 70% low income and 30% very low income, with recorded covenants; density bonus units per state law (55 years for rental).
record.next_deadline: Not applicable; ministerial. Unincorporated communities include Midway City, Rossmoor, North Tustin, Ladera Ranch, Rancho Mission Viejo, Silverado and El Modena. Confirm site eligibility with OC Development Services; processing fee deposit applies.
record.layering_notes: The overlay matters because most of the County's own land-use authority covers small pockets; the 2026 NOFA gives unincorporated overlay sites the first 60-day application window and the higher $137,500 per unit subsidy. Density bonus and by-right approval do not trigger prevailing wage. Manual PDF opened on ocds.ocpublicworks.com; zoning code mirror on Zoneomics shows section headings and overlay affordability terms.

record.program_name: Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA), City of Santa Ana entitlement
record.administering_agency: City of Santa Ana Community Development Agency, Housing Division
record.typical_award_size: Amount not published on the City site. The 2021-2029 Housing Element lists PLHA alongside Inclusionary and HOME as a funding source for the City's rental production, acquisition-rehabilitation and homeownership programs, and the City's own HHAP allocation is budgeted separately. The Housing Division Quarterly Report (FY 2025-26 Q4) does not list PLHA among available development funds, which suggests the allocation is committed to homeless services and homeownership rather than offered to developers.
record.affordability_requirement: Per PLHA statute: rental production at or below 60% AMI, assistance to persons experiencing homelessness, affordable ownership and workforce housing.
record.next_deadline: unknown, verify with agency; confirm the five-year PLHA plan allocation and whether any PLHA is set aside for development.
record.layering_notes: Santa Ana is an HCD PLHA entitlement separate from the County Urban County allocation (County CY 2025 $956,505), and its share is likely larger than the County's, but no City page or report with the figure could be opened this pass; santa-ana.gov site search returned no PLHA page. Treat as a possible add-on to the Housing Division RFP rather than a stand-alone source. Housing Element PDF (September 2022 certified element) opened and is the source for the program description.

record.program_name: City-owned and Housing Authority-owned site solicitations for affordable housing (Beach Boulevard corridor and Center City developer RFPs)
record.administering_agency: Anaheim Housing Authority and Housing and Community Development Department, Real Property and Housing Development staff
record.typical_award_size: Land contributions under long-term ground leases plus City gap loans rather than a cash NOFA: Miraflores (85 units) on a 60-year City ground lease with a $3,000,000 HOME loan; Southeast Corner of Beach and Lincoln (46 affordable senior and transition-age youth units) on former Housing Authority land with 46 PBVs; earlier RFPs for 212 S. Beach Blvd (Silvermoon) and State College at Lincoln (about 0.51 acre) sought developers for lower income and special needs housing. The A-LHTF Build More Homes Initiative funds site acquisition for future solicitations.
record.affordability_requirement: Project-specific: City solicitations have required 100% affordable or supportive housing with 55-year covenants and local resident preference.
record.next_deadline: unknown, verify with agency; no open RFP was located this pass. Watch Housing Authority agendas for Beach Boulevard parcels (Anaheim Lodge demolition site, 39 Commons remainder).
record.layering_notes: The most valuable Anaheim resource is land, not cash: the Housing Authority assembled Beach Boulevard motel sites and the City leases them at nominal rent, which replaces a $5,000,000 to $10,000,000 land cost in a 4% deal. Pair with Housing Authority PBVs, HOME or PLHA loans, A-LHTF gap money and County MHSA/BHSA. The RFP pages and Authority agendas could not be opened (anaheim.gov CivicAlerts and DocumentCenter returned 403; Granicus archive lists meetings but not staff reports), so details are from the A-LHTF Guidelines, the Housing Authority page and the 2026 fact sheet.

record.program_name: Affordable Housing In-Lieu Fee Fund (Irvine Zoning Ordinance Sec. 2-3-5.B.3.c; fee set by City Council resolution)
record.administering_agency: City of Irvine Community Development Department
record.typical_award_size: In-lieu fees are deposited in the City's affordable housing fund and used for projects serving low, very low and extremely low income households and Housing Element needs; the fee is set by Council resolution and determined at building permit (a legacy $17,000 per unit rate applied only to Irvine Business Complex projects filed before 2007). An Affordable Housing Requirement and In-Lieu Fee Update draft study was posted August 3, 2023 (per the City page title captured in search results), but the adopted schedule and the current fund balance could not be read because cityofirvine.gov blocked access. The City's FY 2023-25 budget reported a four-acre land conveyance to the Irvine Community Land Trust as part of its 100% affordable housing support.
record.affordability_requirement: Fund uses limited to low, very low and extremely low income households and Housing Element implementation; recipients record 55-year covenants under Chapter 2-3.
record.next_deadline: unknown, verify with agency; no NOFA located. Ask Community Development for the current in-lieu fee resolution, fund balance and whether a developer round is planned.
record.layering_notes: Because most Irvine builders provide units on-site or through credits, the in-lieu fund is smaller than Santa Ana's; its visible use is land and loans to Irvine Community Land Trust projects (Salerno, Parc Derian, Doria, Alegre, Sage Park) which then take LIHTC, HOME, OCHFT and County MHSA money. Public funds trigger state prevailing wage. Code section read on zoneomics; City pages (node 81916 and affordable housing pages) returned 403.
eligible_project_detail: land for Irvine Community Land Trust projects

record.program_name: Affordable Housing Credits Program (Irvine Zoning Ordinance Sec. 2-3-6)
record.administering_agency: City of Irvine Community Development Department (credits database and three-party credits agreements)
record.typical_award_size: Market mechanism, not a subsidy. Projects that build more affordable units than the 15% requirement earn transferable credits in three income categories (extremely low or very low, low, moderate) that they may sell to market-rate projects or mixed projects with a shortfall; credits become available after building permits are issued for the excess units and a completion bond or certificate of occupancy is in place. A three-party credits agreement (buyer, seller, City) must be executed before the buyer's building permits; sale prices are not disclosed to the City.
record.affordability_requirement: Credits track the income level of the excess units; the receiving project satisfies its required affordable component at that level.
record.next_deadline: Agreement before building permit; City maintains the credits database on request.
record.layering_notes: For a 100% affordable developer this is a revenue source unique among the five Orange County priority cities: excess units can be monetized to market-rate builders in the same or other planning areas, effectively a private in-lieu payment. Confirm with the City how many credits are outstanding and the recent trading range. Read on the zoneomics mirror because cityofirvine.gov returned 403.

record.program_name: Affordable Housing and Permanent Supportive Housing Development RFP and Housing Element Program 4 (Affordable Housing Construction assistance)
record.administering_agency: City of Garden Grove Community and Economic Development Department, Neighborhood Improvement Division and Housing Authority
record.typical_award_size: The City posted a developer solicitation (gg.city/afford-rfp, redirecting to the Neighborhood Improvement page for the Affordable Housing and Permanent Supportive Housing Development RFP) seeking qualified developers to build affordable and permanent supportive housing units; the page returned 403 to all fetch methods so the funding amount, sites and deadline could not be read. Housing Element Program 4 commits the City to technical and financial assistance for about 10 affordable units a year (80 units over the cycle) through land cost write-downs and construction assistance from General Fund, HOME, LMIHAF and PLHA, plus expedited processing. The FY 2025-30 Consolidated Plan earmarks part of about $2,900,000 of HOME-ARP for one PSH development, and the Housing Successor is buying the Civic Center Parcel for housing.
record.affordability_requirement: Program 4 targets lower income and senior households; HOME-ARP PSH units serve qualifying homeless populations; 55-year covenants under Sec. 9.60.050 regulatory agreements.
record.next_deadline: unknown, verify with agency; confirm whether the Affordable Housing and PSH Development RFP is still open and whether it covers the Civic Center Parcel. Contact Neighborhood Improvement (714-741-5144).
record.layering_notes: Likely the only Garden Grove developer solicitation and probably paired with HOME-ARP and LMIHAF land; a respondent should plan on County 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA loans, OCHFT, County BHSA and GGHA PBVs for the rest of the stack. Public funds trigger state prevailing wage. Source is the 2021-2029 Housing Element PDF (opened); the RFP page itself was blocked (ggcity.org/news/afford-rfp and the neighborhood-improvement RFP page both 403).
